raw_case_text:
A 24-year-old previously healthy male soldier experienced an upper respiratory tract infection (URI) 2 weeks prior to his presentation. One week after the infection subsided, he had dysphagia, truncal and limb ataxia, and symmetrical proximal muscles weakness. On the third day of his neurological illness, total ophthalmoplegia, cerebellar dysarthria, and generalized hyporeflexia were evidenced at a primary hospital, and then, he was immediately transferred to our hospital. He had never been exposed to food or substances containing neurological toxins. On admission to our center, the weakness of limbs and respiratory muscles progressed rapidly to flaccid quadriparesis, which was dominant in the upper limbs, and respiratory muscle paralysis so that mechanical ventilation was indicated. All deep tendon reflexes were absent. Nevertheless, his consciousness, pinprick sensation, and proprioception were absolutely intact. MFS and GBS overlap syndrome was a provisional diagnosis at initial evaluation. The GBS disability score at that time was 5. Medical Research Council sum score was 44; the muscle strength was symmetrical as follows: both shoulders abduction 3; elbow flexion 3; wrist extension 4; hip flexion 4; knee flexion 4, and ankle dorsiflexion 4.
The results of routine blood chemistry tests, anti-HIV, anti-HBV, anti-HCV, as well as a panel of serology tests of autoimmune disorders were unremarkable. The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed clear CSF, normal pressure, and no blood cells. The CSF/serum glucose ratio was 83/110 mg/dL. CSF protein was 74.9 mg/dL. CSF culture and polymerase chain reaction for possible organisms, such as bacteria, mycobacterium tuberculosis, herpes viruses, Japanese B virus, and Dengue viruses, yielded negative results. The electroneuromyographic (ENMG) study showed symmetrical sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy, which was dominant in both upper limbs. Left facial axonal neuropathy was detected as well (Fig. 1). A panel of AGAbs, including anti-GM1, -GM2, -GM3, -GD1a, -GD1b, -GT1b, and -GQ1b, was negative. Based on the clinical presentation and ENMG results, MFS/AMSAN-GBS overlap syndrome was the final diagnosis, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy was immediately initiated. The neurological symptoms dramatically resolved 4 days after the treatment. GBS disability score became 2 eventually.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 24-year-old male soldier presented with a 3-day history of dysphagia, truncal and limb ataxia, symmetrical proximal muscle weakness, total ophthalmoplegia, and cerebellar dysarthria 1 week after an upper respiratory tract infection.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One week after resolution of an upper respiratory tract infection (2 weeks prior to presentation), the previously healthy soldier developed dysphagia, truncal and limb ataxia, and symmetrical proximal muscle weakness, followed on day 3 of neurological symptoms by complete external ophthalmoplegia, cerebellar dysarthria, and generalized hyporeflexia, rapidly progressing on admission to upper-limb-predominant flaccid quadriparesis, areflexia, and respiratory muscle paralysis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy soldier; upper respiratory tract infection 2 weeks prior; no neurotoxin exposure.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for antecedent URI, dysphagia, diplopia/ophthalmoplegia, dysarthria, truncal/limb ataxia, rapidly progressive four-limb weakness, and respiratory distress.

objective.physical_examination: Intact consciousness, pinprick sensation, and proprioception; total bilateral ophthalmoplegia, cerebellar dysarthria, left facial nerve weakness, symmetrical upper-limb-predominant flaccid quadriparesis (MRC sum score 44: bilateral shoulder abduction 3/5, elbow flexion 3/5, wrist extension 4/5, hip flexion 4/5, knee flexion 4/5, ankle dorsiflexion 4/5; GBS disability score 5), global absence of deep tendon reflexes, truncal/limb ataxia, and respiratory muscle paralysis requiring mechanical ventilation.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine blood chemistry, anti-HIV, anti-HBV, anti-HCV, autoimmune serology panel, and serum antiganglioside antibody panel (anti-GM1, -GM2, -GM3, -GD1a, -GD1b, -GT1b, -GQ1b) were all negative/normal. Electroneuromyography (ENMG) demonstrated symmetrical upper-limb-predominant sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy and left facial axonal neuropathy.
objective.advanced_workup: CSF analysis revealed albuminocytologic dissociation with clear acellular fluid (0 cells), normal opening pressure, CSF protein 74.9 mg/dL, CSF/serum glucose 83/110 mg/dL, and negative CSF bacterial culture and PCR for M. tuberculosis, herpesviruses, Japanese encephalitis B virus, and dengue viruses.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Miller Fisher syndrome and acute motor-sensory axonal neuropathy Guillain-Barre syndrome (MFS/AMSAN-GBS) overlap syndrome, confirmed by clinical triad (ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia) plus axonal sensorimotor quadriparesis on ENMG and CSF albuminocytologic dissociation. Dengue virus was ruled out by negative CSF dengue PCR. Treated with mechanical ventilation and immediate intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy, achieving dramatic neurological improvement within 4 days and recovery to a GBS disability score of 2.
